topic: The AMD llama.cpp fork story: community patch set, retired AMD repo, Radeon options
title: The AMD fork that is not from AMD
description: The AMD llama.cpp fork everyone is sharing is not AMD's. AMD's own fork is retired, and the trending speedup is one maintainer's nineteen-patch set for stock llama.cpp. You'll learn what stock llama.cpp already does on Radeon via HIP and Vulkan, and what the patch set really adds. (Narration is AI-generated.)
hook_text: You speed up your Radeon tonight.

narration_full: You speed up your Radeon tonight. Then you check who built it. Your Radeon already runs llama.cpp, the free local AI engine. Then an AMD fork, a copy you change yourself, tops Hacker News. AMD's own fork is retired, pointing to the original. The speedup is llama-cpp-rdna-boosts, one maintainer's patches for stock code. Step one: clone the llama.cpp repository. Step two: pin the commit and apply the patches. Step three: build it for your Radeon. Nineteen patches now live in your engine. One author's Radeon made thirty-five tokens a second, how fast answers appear. Patched, it hit fifty-five tokens a second. Yours may differ. AMD's fix remains a proposal; your speedup came from one outsider's patches.

analogy.mapping: stock llama.cpp is the engine everyone gets; llama-cpp-rdna-boosts is a tuner's kit of 19 patches bolted onto one pinned production run; AMD's own fork is the discontinued in-house tuning shop whose door now says use the stock engine
analogy.limit: the tune is 19 software patches by one person, re-fitted at every re-base, and the advertised gains are one driver's stopwatch, not a dyno sheet
